title: Embedding inference: reduce tail latency via micro-batch windowing and kernel tuning
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: reduce embedding endpoint tail latency (p95/p99) while keeping or improving throughput and embedding quality. We will experiment with micro-batching window strategies, per-device kernel selection, and lightweight request prioritization to reduce tail events caused by variance in sequence length and kernel scheduling. Deliverables: benchmark harness, kernel parameter matrix, telemetry dashboards showing before/after p50/p95/p99, canary rollout plan with automatic fallback to slower but more predictable kernels.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for 512-token embedding workload reduced by >= 30% compared to baseline (measured on dedicated-staging GPUs)
no degradation in embedding cosine-similarity AUC on validation set (delta < 0.5% compared to baseline)
end-to-end throughput for mixed small/large requests remains within 5% of baseline or improves
automated Canary rollout and rollback hooks implemented in runtime with dashboard-linked alerts
comments: 2025-03-12 Sofia Patel: Created ticket after postmortem of multiple customer reports showing p99 spikes for embedding routes under mixed workloads. Initial hypothesis: variance in sequence length + kernel dispatch causes long tail; micro-batching windowing may smooth but could harm latency for small requests.

2025-03-15 Aisha Khan: Completed minimal benchmark harness that replays production trace (sampled) against staging cluster. Baseline numbers: p50=18ms, p95=120ms, p99=350ms for mixed 0-1024 token distribution on A6000 equivalent. Uploaded trace and harness to Confluence.

2025-03-18 Rahul Mehta (ML infra): Ran kernel matrix sweep for int8 and fp16 paths. Observed that kernel K-7 has 15% lower throughput on long sequences but 25% lower tail variance. Proposal: route long sequences to K-7 and short ones to K-3 with dynamic kernel selection in scheduler.

2025-03-22 Design review (internal): PM raised concern about increased cost if dynamic routing increases GPU utilization; agreed to add cost metric to dashboards and make routing configurable per-customer/tier.

2025-03-25 Aisha Khan: Implemented micro-batch window with max-delay=3ms and max-batch=64; initial replay lowered p95 by 12% but p99 unchanged. Hypothesis: a small subset of large requests create head-of-line blocking. Added small-request prioritization in scheduler which preempts micro-batch if single-request latency would exceed threshold.

2025-03-28 SRE comment: Canary jobs show improved p99 from 350ms to 210ms on staging with prioritization + kernel routing. Observed 4% increase in overall GPU utilization. Created alert rule: if cost increase >10% rollback automatically.

2025-03-30 Code review feedback from Marco Liu: Ensure fallback to conservative kernel for cold-cache cases and add a telemetry tag for "kernel_routing_reason" to enable post-hoc analysis of decisions. Also requested integration test that replays long-sequence spike scenarios.

2025-04-02 Aisha Khan: Opened PR for scheduler changes and kernel routing (PR 1768). Benchmarks attached in PR show p99=190ms, p95=95ms for the replayed trace; embedding quality metrics (cosine AUC) unchanged within noise. Moving to canary rollout Wednesday 2025-04-08.

2025-04-02 Product note (Sofia Patel): PM approved canary with 10% traffic on dedicated-staging then 50% on the dedicated pool. Will collect 72h of telemetry focused on tail bins and cost delta before wider rollout. If p99 improvement <25% or cost >8% we rollback.
